I'm 66 this year, been farming since I was 16 — that's 50 years on this same land in Quzhou. It's just me and my old lady now, two of us trying to get by on 5 mu. Our son and daughter-in-law work over in Handan; they send a bit when they can, but we can't count on it. I've got enough schooling to read the numbers on a fertilizer bag and follow what the extension fellow says at the village meeting, but at the end of the day I trust what I've seen with my own eyes.

This year I'm keeping it simple: **4 mu of cotton** and **1 mu of mungbean**. Cotton is my cash crop — I need that money for living expenses, my blood pressure medicine, and to fix the roof if it leaks again. Mungbean is my insurance: it's easy to manage, we eat mungbean noodles and sprouts all year, and if cotton prices collapse again, at least I'll have something.

### Cotton (4 mu)

I'll plant around **April 22nd to 25th**, right after Grain Rain when the soil warms up. I'm buying **Bt cotton seed** from the county supply store for about 35 yuan per mu. I used to save my own seed, but these bollworm-resistant varieties really do save me sprays, and with just the two of us, every trip to the field matters. I'll rotary till with my walking tractor — I still handle it fine, though my back complains more than it used to — then rake the furrows by hand.

For fertilizer, the extension agent keeps saying I should do soil testing and push nitrogen to 18 kg per mu, but I've got 50 years of experience on this exact plot and I know it doesn't need that much. I'm putting down **one 40 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu** as base at planting. When the first flowers show in early July, I'll topdress **15 kg of urea per mu**. If the plants look dark green and vigorous, I might cut that to 10 kg — save a few yuan. Last year I did 15 kg and it was fine, so probably 15 kg again. I can't afford to waste money on fertilizer I don't need, but I also can't afford a yield drop. Better a little too much than too little.

I'll irrigate **three times**: once right after planting to help germination, once at peak flowering in mid-July when the heat hits, and once during boll filling in August. Water from the tube well cooperative costs about 10 yuan per mu each time, so three times is 120 yuan total for the 4 mu. Four times would be better in a drought year, but that's another 40 yuan I don't have. Three has been enough most years.

Pesticides are non-negotiable for cotton. I spray a **pre-emergence herbicide** before planting, then **insecticide** three or four times through the season. I watch the plants every morning — if I see bollworm eggs or aphids clustering, I spray that week. The Bt cotton helps, but I don't trust it alone. I budget about 150 yuan per mu for chemicals.

The hard part is **labor**. Planting, thinning, pruning — my wife and I can manage that together. But come September and October, picking cotton by hand is backbreaking work, and at my age I can't bend like that all day anymore. I'll have to hire women from the village to help pick. I usually pay by the weight — about 2 yuan per kilogram of seed cotton. At 280 kg per mu across 4 mu, that's a big cash outlay, but I have no choice. Between planting, managing, and picking, I'll put in about 80 days of my own labor, and hire maybe 15 days of help.

I expect about **280 kg of seed cotton per mu** if the weather cooperates. Last year I got 275 kg. The year before, a late drought knocked me down to 240 kg. I don't dare hope for more than 280.

### Mungbean (1 mu)

I plant mungbean on the eastern mu around **early May**, after cotton is settled. I put a **small amount of compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting** — maybe 15 kg per mu — and that's it. Mungbean doesn't need much. I might irrigate once in June if the drought is severe, but usually I don't bother. It's a short crop, ready by August. I'll harvest about **100 kg per mu**, enough for our own table and maybe a few hundred yuan if I sell the surplus. It only takes about 5 days of our labor total.

### The tradeoffs

Every yuan I spend on cotton fertilizer is a yuan I don't have for hiring pickers. Every extra irrigation helps the yield but drains my cash. I thought about planting all 5 mu in cotton to maximize income, but at my age, managing 5 mu of cotton alone would break me — and if bollworm hit or prices crashed, we'd have nothing to eat. The mungbean stays. I'm running down my savings by about 3,600 yuan this season, which makes me nervous, but cotton should bring in around 7,800 yuan gross if I hit my yield target. After all costs, we'll survive another year. That's all I'm asking for.
